The text says one may reduce to normalA and reports characteristic-zero and essentially-finite-type positive cases, but ignorance even for completeA,B with trivial residue extension.
reconstruction: The intended question is about reduced/integralA (the preceding discussion concerns integrality). Modern geometric unibranchness alone permits nilpotents, so literal wording without reducedness has the elementary counterexample A=B=k[ε]/ε². That counterexample does not settle the intended normal-base question.
check_reason: The exact open question, known cases and cancellation are retained. It is not dismissed merely because the paper is reused.

statement: The draft gives an integral complete real node A=R[[X,Y]]/(X²+Y²), unibranch but not geometrically unibranch; its finite étale complexification is not integral, because X²+Y²=(X+iY)(X−iY). It also describes a nodal-curve étale example.
reconstruction: Double brackets are a reconstruction from “complet”; the diplomatic notation leaves them blank. The algebraic point explains why ordinary unibranchness is insufficient. The real quadratic has no real linear factors, so the completed plane-curve quotient is a domain.
check_reason: The counterexample is mathematically sound with the reconstructed power-series notation; the notation itself remains an ink question.

his_words: Théorème7.5.1; toutes les fibres ... Q géométrique
statement: The cancelled EGA draft proposes a general local-to-all-fibers criterion for a flat local mapA→B with finite residue extension: a local propertyR stable under lifting across regular elements and open on finiteB-algebras, with A universally Japanese and regular generic loci on finite integralA-algebras, ascends geometrically from the closed fiber to all fibers. It lists depth/codepth, Serre, Cohen–Macaulay, regularity, normality, integrality and reducedness variants.
reconstruction: The text alternatesR and Q and has missing relation signs. Final EGAIV2 §7.5 is the comparison target, but each property’s auxiliary hypotheses must be read individually; excellentB is a convenient common sufficient assumption, not an automatic omitted hypothesis.
check_reason: The drafting comment says the old statement was too narrow for what the proof established. Cancellation is recorded without implying that every listed case is false.

statement: A cancelled EGA fragment gives: a length-one hypersurface section criterion for a unique generically reduced component and a regular parameter; reducedness of F from reducedF/tF when V(t) contains no component of SuppF; specialization of associated components under an F-regular t; and descent of the no-embedded-components condition from F/tF to F.
reconstruction: The preceding conditions1/1(ii), the exact definition of a reduced module and the missing inequality are not supplied. Standard local statements can be compared, but a theorem with all original quantifiers cannot be recovered by filling these slots.
check_reason: The last three arguments refer to other numbered results and the visible corollary; a “reste à prouver” followed by that reference is not necessarily a surviving open problem.

his_words: On se gardera de croire ... intersection
statement: Flat finite-type base change need not preserve an infinite intersection of ideals. For a DVR A and J_i=m^i, their intersection is zero, but for B=Frac(A)=A[1/π], every J_iB=B.
reconstruction: B is a flat finite-typeA-algebra (one localization generator). This checks every displayed hypothesis; no faithful-flatness or locality is asserted here.
check_reason: The draft’s counterexample is correct and explains the distinction from finite intersections. Missing intersection symbols are scan alarms.

his_words: Nous ignorons si ... S quelconque; relativement à S; cf SGAD IX4.2
statement: The draft asks whether a schematically dominant family over a field stays so after every base change, defines universal schematic dominance, and states lifting across a nilpotent closed base when X and all Z_i are flat over S. It reports the locally Noetherian case as positive.
reconstruction: EGAIV3 Proposition 11.10.6 answers the arbitrary field-base-change question affirmatively; Definition 11.10.8 and Theorem 11.10.9 organize the relative version. The ordinary nilpotent lemma is false without more hypotheses: for S=Spec Q[x,ε]/(ε²,xε), X=S and Z=D(x), density holds over S_0=Spec Q[x] but fails over S. The opened SGA3II ExposéIX Lemma 4.2 and EGAIV3 11.9.15 require every J^n/J^(n+1) locally free on S_0, which need not itself be reduced.
check_reason: The draft is faithfully recorded, but its ordinary nilpotent assertion is refuted. The field-base-change question is answered in the later publication. The universal-relative variant is kept distinct.

his_words: Formalism of Algebraic Cohomology Classes; ρ_X:C^i(X)→H_l^{2i}(X)
statement: The English reused sheet constructs a rational cycle-class map by trace adjointness to restriction, asserts independence of rational equivalence and multiplicativity, and defines cohomological equivalence as its kernel.
reconstruction: To state it precisely use smooth proper equidimensionalX over an algebraically closed field, ℓ invertible, and Tate twistH^{2i}(X,Q_ℓ(i)); singularZ requires its fundamental class/trace on top compactly supported cohomology, not Poincaré duality on Z. Those hypotheses may belong to missing preceding pages. The author of this English sheet is not identified by an explicit byline.
check_reason: The text assumes a cohomology formalism already established. Merely defining the functional on cycles does not prove rational-equivalence invariance or intersection compatibility; these are separate asserted results.
